newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CVRD studying 1,500 job-cut proposal.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CVRD studying 1,500 job-cut proposal.

text.p: The new controling shareholders of recently privatized Brazilian mining giant CVRD are studying a proposal by company staff for 1,500 job cuts, a CVRD spokesman said.
He said CVRD employees had put forward a proposal for a voluntary redundancy program involving 10 percent of CVRD's current workforce of 15,500 prior to the company's privatization.

The international Valepar consortium, led by Brazilian steelmaker CSN, bought a controling stake in CVRD for $3.15 billion May 6 and has given itself six months to study the company before introducing any changes.
The company is looking at other cost-cutting measures and is currently negotiating a 30-percent reduction in the value of all its contracts with suppliers and service providers, the spokesman said.
He said CVRD was also looking into closing down some of its representative offices abroad.

The new controllers are also reviewing CVRD's management and are likely to name a new company president in the near future given that CVRD's current president, Francisco Schettino, has asked to be dismissed from his duties earlier than planned.
Valepar asked CVRD's directors to continue in their jobs for six months after privatization, but Schettino said he wanted to leave before then.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
